issues.legal_issue: An earlier order limiting the issues in a partition suit does not bar amendment of the property schedule where the order only precludes renewed litigation over the genuineness of a compromise document.
material_facts: An earlier appellate order barred the parties from contesting the genuineness of a compromise document but did not bar trial of the suit or prescribe a special procedure.
The plaintiff sought to correct descriptions of properties in the plaint schedule and add properties said to have been omitted through ignorance.
The amendment was sought before disposal of the suit and before a preliminary decree, and the compromise document did not specify the items of property.
issues.conclusion: The amendment of the plaint was properly allowed; the earlier order did not preclude it.
issues.legal_principle: An order precluding renewed litigation of a document’s genuineness does not, without more, prevent amendment of the pleadings or a trial of the suit. Where property descriptions are incomplete or properties have been omitted, amendment before a preliminary decree may permit those matters to be addressed in the suit rather than left for contested final-decree proceedings. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this ruling.

predicates.partition_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking partition of an estate.
predicates.earlier_order_only_barred_genuineness: An earlier order barred renewed contest over a document’s genuineness but did not bar trial of the suit or prescribe a special procedure for its disposal.
predicates.property_schedule_incomplete: A party claimed that the property schedule contained incorrect or incomplete descriptions or omitted properties.

issues.definition: When a partition suit has an incomplete property schedule and an earlier order only barred renewed contest over a document’s genuineness, amendment of the plaint is permitted.

issues.legal_issue: A preliminary decree should not be passed on the basis of a compromise document when the defendant has not pleaded a claim for such a decree and the suit has not been tried.
material_facts: The defendant did not file a written statement claiming that a decree should be passed in accordance with the compromise document.
No issues had been framed and the suit had not been tried.
The compromise document did not specify the items of property to be allotted.
issues.conclusion: The defendant’s appropriate course was to plead the claim in a written statement and have the suit proceed under the ordinary procedure; a preliminary decree should not have been passed without that pleading and trial.
issues.legal_principle: A party seeking a decree on the basis of a document must plead that relief, after which the trial court is to follow the procedure prescribed for the suit. Here, the Court relied on the absence of a written statement claiming the decree, the absence of framed issues and trial, and the document’s failure to specify the properties. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this ruling.

rule.if: partition_suit and no_written_statement_claiming_decree and no_issues_or_trial and compromise_document_omits_property_items

predicates.partition_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking partition of an estate.
predicates.no_written_statement_claiming_decree: The defendant did not file a written statement seeking a decree on the basis of the compromise document.
predicates.no_issues_or_trial: The court had framed no issues and had conducted no trial of the suit.
predicates.compromise_document_omits_property_items: The compromise document did not identify the items of property to be allotted.

issues.definition: In a partition suit, where the defendant has not pleaded a claim for a decree on a compromise document, no issues or trial have occurred, and the document omits the property items, a preliminary decree is not entered without pleading and trial.
